stem.text: Consider the polar curve \( r = 2 - \cos{\left(\theta \right)} \) for \( 1.7 \le \theta \le 3.55 \). Using a calculator, find the value of \( \theta \) that corresponds to the point on the curve farthest from the x-axis. Justify your answer, show the setup, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The distance from the x-axis is \( |y| \), where \( y = r\sin\theta = \left(2 - \cos{\left(\theta \right)}\right) \sin{\left(\theta \right)} \).

Set \( \frac{dy}{d\theta} = \left(2 - \cos{\left(\theta \right)}\right) \cos{\left(\theta \right)} + \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)} = 0 \). On the interval a calculator gives one solution, \( \theta \approx 1.946 \).

Compare the candidates, the critical angle and both endpoints: \( |y(1.7)| \approx 2.111 \), \( |y(1.946)| \approx 2.202 \), \( |y(3.55)| \approx 1.159 \). The largest distance is at \( \theta \approx 1.946 \), so that is the farthest point.

options.derivation: r treated as the distance from the axis, so the angle where r is largest is reported
the candidates compared correctly but the one nearest the axis reported
the candidates comparison run without the interior critical angle, so the farther endpoint is reported
